Save this.

items.txt__content-bank__19-voice-ai_carousel:
A lead calls at 11 PM on a Saturday. Nobody's there. They still get booked.

That's HighLevel Voice AI: it answers, qualifies and books into the real calendar. Setup matters, so get the persona, script and calendar right.

Comment VOICE.

items.txt__content-bank__24-manual-actions_car:
Manual Actions might be the most underrated step in HighLevel workflows.

It creates a task for a specific teammate: call about the proposal, confirm the appointment. Automate most of it, hand the right part to a human.

Comment SUITE.

#gohighlevel #automation #highlevel #crm
items.card__pod3-08__linkedin:
Horse trainer to AI agency owner.

Ty, 25, from Dallas, got out of horse training after COVID and was in a low spot.
But needing more purpose turned into a digital marketing and automation agency: websites, AI agents, ads and content.
Your old career isn't a dead end. It's the backstory.

#agencyowner #gohighlevel
items.card__pod3-09__threads:
21. Senior at Ohio State. Running an AI consulting company.

Ohaji's mom is a serial entrepreneur, so business was always the plan. The question was which avenue.
Coming from tech, AI was it. Started this past year, and it took off from there.
You don't have to graduate to start.
items.card__pod3-10__linkedin:
Fail forward.

Ty, one of HighLevel's 2026 interns: "If you're gonna fail, fail forward. If you're gonna fall, fall forward."
You will stumble. Just make it a little further than yesterday.
The biggest takeaway from the internship, in Ty's words: resilience and determination.

#resilience #entrepreneurship
items.card__pod3-11__linkedin:
1% better every day.

I asked HighLevel's 2026 interns for one sentence of advice for young founders.
Just do it. Get out there. Be curious. Do hard things.
But the one that stuck: do one small thing every day that makes you better. It stacks up.

#entrepreneurship #founders
items.card__pod3-12__linkedin:
Meet the 2026 HighLevel interns.

Ty left horse training and built an AI agency in Dallas.
McKinley started a YouTube channel at 10 and an agency in high school.
Ohaji is a 21-year-old Ohio State senior running AI consulting.
I sat down with them to talk business and getting started with HighLevel.

#highlevel #entrepreneurship
items.card__pod3-13__linkedin:
Started an agency in high school. Felt like an outcast.

McKinley's friends weren't into business, marketing or content creation.
Nobody made fun of it exactly, but building a business has been a lonely route at times.
If that's you right now, find a room of people building too. They're out there.

#entrepreneurship #founders
items.card__pod3-14__linkedin:
Her saving grace was the community.

One of HighLevel's 2026 interns had the same fears and anxieties as everyone around her.
But seeing someone else put themselves out there changed it.
Therefore she figured: if they can do it, there's no reason I can't.
Who you surround yourself with decides what you're brave enough to do.

#community #contentcreation
items.card__pod3-15__linkedin:
They failed 1,000 times. Then kept going.

McKinley, one of HighLevel's 2026 interns: "The people that are successful in life, they failed a thousand times, but they kept going."
Do hard things often enough and uncomfortable starts to feel normal.
It still sucks. You get through it anyway.

#entrepreneurship #mindset
